description: Sensor pull-mode VM scanning: Sensor dials each VM's agent when that VM is due, optionally forwards a new index report to Central, and retries on NACK. Use this board to see whether jitter and the per-tick start cap pace Central sends, and whether scrapes are failing or only unchanged.

options.content:
Sensor **pulls** index reports: VMScraper ticks, dials each due VM's roxagent over VSOCK, and forwards a successful report through `vmIndex.Handler` to Central. Central ACK/NACKs. Handler enqueue metrics are a secondary "send to Central" story, not the scrape scheduler.

```
  roxagent (in VM)                    Sensor                         Central
  ┌──────────────┐     VSOCK      ┌──────────────┐   SensorEvent   ┌─────────┐
  │ GetReport   │◄───────────────│  VMScraper  │────────────────►│ VM pipe │
  └──────────────┘   when due     │ per-VM next │                 └────┬────┘
                                 │ AttemptAt   │                      │
                                 └──────┬──────┘              SensorACK│
                                        │                    ACK | NACK│
                                        └──────────────────────────────┘
                                   NACK: clear report_generation, shared backoff
```

**Load spreading** (read `pollInterval` from Sensor env; do not assume 5m):

- First wave / Sensor restart: a newly tracked VM gets `nextAttemptAt = now + U(0, C)` where `C = min(20m, pollInterval/3)`.
- Success and permanent failure reschedule at `pollInterval + U(0, W)`, `W = pollInterval × ROX_VIRTUAL_MACHINES_SCRAPER_STEADY_SPREAD_FRACTION` (default 2/3).
- Per-tick start cap (backstop when jitter still lines VMs up): `min(concurrency, max(1, ceil(nDue × tick / C)))`. Leftovers stay due for the next tick. `nDue` is the eligible pile at tick start, not the tracked fleet. Concurrency (default 20) is a separate overlap cap on the errgroup.
- Retryable pull failures and NACKs share exponential backoff (`initialBackoff` default 10s, doubled, cap `min(pollInterval, 30m)`).

Defaults: tick 10s, poll 5m, C 100s, W 200s, concurrency 20. A 4h poll uses C 20m and W 2h40m. First-wave `U(0, C)` is not exported as a histogram; only cadence `U(0, W)` is.

panels.description: How many VMs Sensor is currently scheduling. Poll-interval advice uses this fleet size. The per-tick start cap uses how many are due, not this number.
panels.title: Tracked VMs

panels.description: How many VMs were eligible to scrape on the most recent tick, before the start cap. A high number with ~1 start per tick is the cap draining a backlog. Zero means the next attempts are still in the future.
panels.title: Due VMs (last tick)

panels.description: Lifetime count of full index reports Sensor sent to Central. Unchanged pulls are not included. A Sensor restart resets the counter to 0.
panels.title: Successful forwards to Central

panels.description: Lifetime count of scrapes where the agent had nothing newer than last time. Sensor still talked to the VM; Central did not get a new report. This is the usual case between mandatory refreshes.
panels.title: Unchanged pulls

panels.description: How many times Central rejected a VM index report. Sensor clears the cached generation and retries on a short backoff. The reason (Scanner down, and so on) is in Central logs, not in this number.
panels.title: NACKs from Central

panels.description: How often the scraper loop wakes up. Default 10s tick is about 0.1 per second. A drop to zero means the loop is not running.
panels.title: Tick rate

panels.description: Running total of full index reports Sensor sent to Central (rox_sensor_vsock_pull_requests_total{status="success"}). Each step up is one or more forwards. A paced wave is a run of +1 steps a few seconds apart. A dump is one large jump. A Sensor restart resets the counter to 0. Unchanged pulls are not counted.
panels.title: Successful forwards to Central

panels.description: How many VMs Sensor is scheduling, as a time series. The start cap is computed from the due pile, not from this series.
panels.title: Fleet size

panels.description: Eligible VMs versus how many scrapes that tick actually started. Healthy catch-up with the start cap: due stays high, starts stay near 1. Jitter-only (no cap): due and starts move together. A dump: both jump toward the fleet. Starts are only recorded on ticks that had someone due; idle ticks are omitted.
panels.title: Due pile vs starts per tick

panels.description: Time on X, how many VMs started in that tick on Y, color = how often that happened. Only ticks that had at least one due VM are recorded, so there is no 0 row. Cap 1 should glow on Y near 1. A bright band at Y near the fleet (or 20) is a dump. Compare Tick rate if most wall-clock ticks are idle.
panels.title: Starts per tick heatmap

panels.description: How many observed ticks started 1, 2, 3, ... VMs. Idle ticks (nobody due) are not sampled, so there is no 0 bar; those ticks show up on Tick rate instead. For a small fleet with start cap 1, mass should sit in 1. Mass in 8 or 20 is a dump.
panels.title: Starts per tick distribution

panels.description: Time on X, gap between consecutive Central sends on Y (seconds), color = how often that gap occurred. This is Sensor-wide, not per VM, and only full forwards (not unchanged pulls). A paced wave is a bright band around the tick (default ~10s). A dump is bright near 0s. Long quiet stretches between waves are normal.
panels.title: Forward interarrival heatmap

panels.description: Typical (P50) and large (P90/P99) gaps between consecutive Central sends over time. With few forwards the lines jump; histogram_quantile on a sparse rate() window can pin to ~0. Prefer the heatmap and distribution for gap size.
panels.title: Forward interarrival percentiles

panels.description: How many Central-send gaps fell in each size bucket over the selected range. Mass in 0.08s or less means reports left Sensor almost together (a dump). Mass around 10-41s is a paced wave at a 10s tick. Mass in minutes-or-more is idle time between waves, which is normal when guests are unchanged.
panels.title: Forward interarrival distribution

panels.description: Time on X, extra random delay added on top of the poll interval on Y. Recorded only when a VM returns to cadence after a successful scrape or a permanent failure. First-wave U(0, C) jitter and NACK/retry backoff are not on this chart. Empty after Sensor start until the first cadence reschedule. A uniform draw on [0, W] should fill the band, not pile on 0.
panels.title: Schedule offset heatmap

panels.description: Typical extra delay on return-to-cadence, over time. Empty until the first success or permanent-failure reschedule. NACK retries will not move this chart. P50 should sit near W/2 (2/3 of poll / 2).
panels.title: Schedule offset percentiles

panels.description: Totals of those extra delays over the selected range. Default poll 5m piles around 0-200s. A 4h poll piles under ~2h40m (W). This is the random band on the next poll, not the gap between Central forwards.
panels.title: Schedule offset distribution

panels.description: Rate of scrape results. success = new report sent to Central. unchanged = agent had nothing new. The rest are errors (dial, timeout, not_ready, busy, and so on). Retryable errors should continue at backoff, not at 1 per tick for the whole fleet.
panels.title: Pull outcomes by status

panels.description: Rate of Central acknowledgements. NACKs with ongoing success means Sensor is resending full reports after a reject. The NACK reason is in Central logs.
panels.title: ACK vs NACK

panels.description: Good pulls (success + unchanged) versus retryable errors versus permanent failures. A retryable stack as large as fleet times 1/tick is a tight loop, not backoff.
panels.title: Retryable errors vs success+unchanged

panels.description: Running totals of Central ACK vs NACK. A climbing NACK line plus continued success is retry-after-reject, not a silent stall.
panels.title: ACK / NACK cumulative

panels.description: Time to connect to the agent, time to read the report, and end-to-end (dial + read + send). A high read P99 with a healthy dial points at a slow agent, not a VSOCK connect problem. Total is only recorded on successful forwards.
panels.title: Pull latency: dial / read / total

panels.description: How long a tick spent waiting on the scrapes it started. If this sits well above the configured tick (default 10s), the ticker is falling behind and the due pile can grow even when the start cap is 1 per tick.
panels.title: Tick duration

panels.description: Size of forwarded reports (not unchanged pulls). Watch this against the 16MB response ceiling. Climbing multi-MB P95 is early warning before rejects.
panels.title: Report payload bytes

panels.description: Package count in forwarded reports. Use with payload bytes when a report is oversized.
panels.title: Packages per report

panels.description: Tick rate should stay about 1 per tick interval. Starts-per-tick samples are fewer because idle ticks are omitted. A large gap between the two means most ticks had an empty due pile (steady state), not a broken histogram.
panels.title: Ticks vs starts-per-tick samples

panels.description: After a successful pull, Handler sends to Central. This is dequeue/send outcomes (success, unknown VM, and so on), not the scrape scheduler.
panels.title: Handler processing rate by outcome

panels.description: Handler's send counter. If this diverges from pull success, the scrape worked but enqueue/send did not.
panels.title: Handler reports sent to Central

panels.description: Time spent waiting because the Handler channel was full. Spreading should keep this near zero. Rising P95 means Central/Handler cannot drain as fast as VMScraper forwards.
panels.title: Handler blocking enqueue percentiles

panels.description: How often that channel was full. A climb is Handler/Central backpressure, not a due-pile dump by itself.
panels.title: Enqueue blocked count

panels.description: Time from dequeue to a successful Central send. Spikes here can fill the enqueue channel even when scrape spreading is healthy.
panels.title: Handler processing duration (success)

title: VM Index Report - Sensor Metrics
